Save the results of a run

Source: R/save_results.R
save_results.Rd

save_results() writes one results object for each scenario and simulation of a run, and stacks the simulations. It checks the fake scenarios with their expect_ functions, and writes nothing when an object fails check_results().

Usage

save_results(r, p, scenarios, gitexclude = NULL)

Arguments

r

The value of run_plan() for the plan p.

p

The plan, with data from add_data() and analyses from add_analyses().

scenarios

The scenarios of the run, from scenarios(). They MUST be the scenarios of the analyses of p.

gitexclude

NULL, or the names of the analysis kinds whose results hold data for each person. See the section Two files.

Value

Invisibly, a data.frame of every assertion, with the columns scenario, assertion, expected, observed and pass.

Details

Call initialize_project() first. For each scenario and simulation, save_results() builds one results object, a named list. Its first element is manifest. When a data function returned a cohort::CohortPipeline, the next element is exclusions, the exclusion tables of the cohorts row-bound in the order of add_data(). The column data names the data of each row. The section A cohort as the data of add_data() gives the columns. A plan without a cohort has no element exclusions. Then comes one element for each analysis kind of add_analyses(), under the kind name and in the order of the calls. The scenario "real" has no element of a kind with control = TRUE. The element of a kind holds the values of its analyses for that scenario and simulation, in the order of the plan:

  • When each value is a data.frame, the element is the values row-bound. Each extra dimension of the kind comes first as a column, unless the data.frame has a column of that name already. A data.table stays a data.table. A kind without extra dimensions has the data.frame of its one analysis.

  • Otherwise, a kind without extra dimensions has the value of its one analysis.

  • Otherwise, the element is a named list with one entry for each analysis. Each name is <name>__<i>, the analysis name without the scenario and the simulation. So the names are the same in each simulation. add_analyses() gives the order of <i>.

The manifest is a list with these elements:

  • pbn_version and r_version.

  • packages, a named character vector. The names are the attached and loaded packages of this R session that are not base packages, and the values are their versions. qs2 is always in the list, because it writes the file.

  • run_date, the date of the call as YYYY-MM-DD. It has no time, so two runs on one day with the same inputs and packages write the same bytes.

  • version, scenario, sim and sims.

  • settings, the named list of the setting columns of the scenario. It is an empty list when there are none.

  • source_md5, the md5 of <version>_run.R and of each file in <version>_functions/, named by the path relative to home. initialize_project() computes it before it sources the files. The rule manifest_source needs the run script in it, so save_results() stops when <version>_run.R did not exist.

  • For the scenario "real" only, data_md5, the md5 of each file directly in data_raw when run_plan() started. So it names the data that the run read, also after a change of a file since initialize_project(). save_results() stops for "real" when data_raw did not exist when initialize_project() ran.

  • For a fake scenario only, fake_md5, one md5 of the code of the data functions of add_data(), without their source references. A change in a function that a data function calls does not change fake_md5. source_md5 holds the md5 of the files of those functions.

  • n_rows_data, a named integer vector with the number of rows of each data element. A list of data.frames with one number of rows, for example a list of imputed data sets, has the rows of one of them. Each other element that is not a data.frame has NA. The analysis <scenario>__sim_<kkkk>__pbn_n_rows of add_analyses() counts them where the data is, also on a worker. The rule no_row_per_person reads it.

  • n_rows_before_exclusions, a named integer vector with the number of rows given to the cohort of each data element, or NA for data without a cohort. no_row_per_person reads it too.

  • n_rows_after_exclusions, the same for the rows after the exclusions: n_after of the last step of the exclusion table. It has a number also when n_rows_data is NA, for example for a mids object.

  • analyses, a data.frame with the columns analysis, control and file: the analysis kinds in the object, and the file of each, "results.qs2" or "results_gitexclude.qs2".

  • data_cache, a data.frame with one row for each data element of add_data() and the columns data, cache, from_cache and cache_key. cache is the argument of add_data(). from_cache is TRUE when run_plan() read the data from the cache. cache_key is the md5 of the cache key, or NA without a cache.

save_results() does these steps in this order. It stops at the first step that fails:

  1. It checks its arguments. It stops when r has no stamp of run_plan() for p. It stops when the settings of scenarios are not the settings in the argsets of p. It stops when a fake scenario has no function expect_<scenario>(results) in the environment of initialize_project(), or when an analysis of r failed. It writes nothing then.

  2. It builds every results object, and the stacked object of each scenario with more than 1 simulation, and checks each with check_results(). On a failure, it prints each failed rule with cat(), writes nothing and stops.

  3. For each scenario, it replaces check.csv with one failed assertion, not checked yet, so that read_results() refuses the new results until step 4 checks them. It writes <version>_results/<scenario>/results.qs2 for 1 simulation. For more simulations, it writes <version>_results/<scenario>/sim_<kkkk>/results.qs2 for each, and then the stacked <version>_results/<scenario>/results.qs2. The section Stacking gives the rules. The files of the scenarios that are not in scenarios stay as they are.

  4. For each scenario with a function expect_<scenario>(), it calls that function on the results of the scenario. expect_real() is optional. The function MUST return a data.frame with at least one row and the columns assertion, expected, observed and pass. save_results() writes it to <version>_results/<scenario>/check.csv and prints it. For "real" without expect_real(), it deletes check.csv. An error, zero rows or another shape is one failed assertion. This rule is the same for expect_real() and for the fake scenarios. save_results() writes check.csv to a temporary file in the same folder and renames it, so a reader never sees a part of it.

  5. After every scenario, it stops when a value of pass is not TRUE. The error lists the failed assertions. The files stay, so that you can find the fault, and read_results() stops on them until the assertions pass.

Stacking

The stacked results hold every element of the results of simulation 1, in the same order. These rules apply at each depth:

  • A data.frame gets a first column sim, and the rows of the simulations in order. It keeps the class of simulation 1, so a data.table stays a data.table.

  • A list is stacked element by element, and pbn matches the elements by name. So each element of a list MUST have its own name.

  • Each other element becomes a list with one entry for each simulation, named sim_0001, sim_0002 and so on. This includes an atomic vector, a matrix, a factor, a date and NULL.

Stacking stops when two simulations differ in the structure at one path, and the error names the path and the two simulations. It also stops on a data.frame with a column sim, because pbn adds that column.

The manifest is that of simulation 1. In it, sim and n_rows_data are NA, sims is the number of simulations, and stacked is TRUE. The columns from_cache and cache_key of data_cache are NA. Stacking stops when the files of the simulations are not exactly the simulations 1 to sims, for example after sims became smaller. Delete the folders of the higher simulations then.

Two files

save_results() writes the results of the kinds in gitexclude to results_gitexclude.qs2, beside each results.qs2. results.qs2 holds manifest, exclusions and every other kind. Use gitexclude for a kind with fitted models, imputations or one row for each person. The project's .gitignore MUST hold the line *gitexclude*, so that git never tracks that file. read_results() reads both files.

These rules apply:

  • save_results() stops before it writes anything when a name in gitexclude is not an analysis kind of p.

  • In a git repository, it also stops when git does not ignore results_gitexclude.qs2.

  • check_results() checks results.qs2 only. So results.qs2 MUST hold an element other than manifest: one kind, or exclusions.

  • The simulations of the two files are stacked apart, with the rules of the section Stacking.

  • Without kinds in gitexclude, save_results() deletes an old results_gitexclude.qs2 of the scenario and of each of its simulations. It prints one line for each deleted file.

vignette("pbn"), which builds and runs a small fake project.

Other results: check_results(), read_results()

Examples

home <- file.path(tempdir(), "pbn_save_example")
dir.create(file.path(home, "v01_functions"), recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(file.path(home, "data"))
writeLines("# The run script.", file.path(home, "v01_run.R"))
writeLines(
  c(
    "CFG <- list(scenarios = data.frame(scenario = c('real', 'null'), sims = 1))",
    "expect_null <- function(results) {",
    "  data.frame(assertion = 'one row', expected = 1,",
    "    observed = nrow(results$means), pass = nrow(results$means) == 1)",
    "}"
  ),
  file.path(home, "v01_functions", "_cfg.R")
)
env <- new.env()
pbn::initialize_project("v01", home, file.path(home, "data"), env = env)
#> You are NOT sourcing into .GlobalEnv. All functions will be sourced into an environment that is returned from this function.
#> Sourcing all code inside /tmp/Rtmp05XhSl/pbn_save_example/v01_functions into 

scenarios <- pbn::scenarios(env$CFG)
p <- plnr::Plan$new()
pbn::add_data(p, "d", fn = function(scenario, sim) {
  return(data.frame(x = stats::rnorm(5)))
})
pbn::add_analyses(p, scenarios, name = "means", fn = function(data, argset) {
  return(data.frame(mean_x = mean(data$d$x)))
})
r <- pbn::run_plan(p)
pbn::save_results(r, p, scenarios)
#> Assertions of the scenario "null":
#>  assertion expected observed pass
#>    one row        1        1 TRUE
names(pbn::read_results("v01", home = home))
#> [1] "manifest" "means"   

unlink(home, recursive = TRUE)
